order.description: with rosetta: the axis ordering to read against, a permutation of the axes (default: the reverse — the transpose)

index.description: with radices or rosetta: the composition's index, a decimal integer of any size

digits.description: with radices: a composition, one choice per position

combinatorics.description: the greatest combination count among the named spaces, with the schema.org microdata of that space: the product as a QuantitativeValue and one ListItem per position, no composition stored (textbook_queneau_compositions)

spaces.description: { name: radices }: many combination spaces counted by the one primitive

hex.description: any hex (a UUID, a hash, an address): presented as a shadcn combination, each nibble an item and a variant, the whole styled from itself — the one quantum core

uuids.description: a UUID-only stream: queried, sorted, filtered and executed by query

neighbours.description: a UUID: its six program-space neighbours, one step on g1, g2 or g3 either way

next.description: a UUID: the program rotated one place, the handle and the tail kept.

navigate.description: a UUID actor: the team it anchors — its six program-space neighbours (g1/g2/g3 either way) and the stream over the neighbourhood (with query, the same stream query); teamwork to the zero bit, a team a neighbourhood a UUID navigates, never a list

query.description: with uuids: { where: { handle, nibble: { at, is }, item, variant, hueBetween }, sort: hex | hue | program | tail, descending, execute }

text.description: the payload: rows as lines (ndjson, csv) fold at rows

bound.description: bytes a piece may hold; e.g.

key.description: a key to locate: the piece it sits in

pieces.description: pieces to unfold: { index, text, sha256? }

withPieces.description: carry the pieces' texts in the answer (default: addresses and hashes only)

integers.description: any paste, one or a list: a digit integer, a minus, a mixed paste, a word, an empty paste.

dna.description: uuid dna uuidna: a DNA sequence (A, C, G, T) as a UUID stream — two bases a nibble, 64 bases a UUID — encoded, addressed and read back one for one, the stream navigable like any UUID stream; a string encodes (A, C, G, T only), { hex } or { uuid } decodes back to bases, { bases } …

reflect.description: the reflective cut: a positive integer (decimal or 0x-hex; or { value, faces? }) cut into faces (2×7 = 14, the mint faces, by default and at most; one a nibble at most), paired i ↔ faces−1−i into σ-witnesses d = u + v, each pair decoded by σ_d(u) = v and σ_d(v) = u from N = u·v …

x-alternatives.says: The inputs of fold are alternatives: one call names one of them, with only the inputs listed beside it under x-alternatives. Two alternatives in one call, or an input beside an alternative it does not combine with, are refused with the code ambiguous_arguments and the names of the inputs at fault.

tools.name: seal
tools.description: SHA-256 of a text, and HMAC-SHA256 under a key the caller gives (a test key; a tenant's secret never travels here), pure and the same at every host; the fold address of the text beside them, so a block, a piece and a message are named by one scheme.

token.description: the widget accepts the credential and sends the sha-256 witness: { witness, via: "widget" }.

pqc.description: Post-quantum cryptography computed: { op: kem-keygen | kem-decapsulate, seed } and { op: kem-encapsulate, publicKey } for X-Wing (ML-KEM-768 with X25519) or, with algorithm, ML-KEM-512, ML-KEM-768 or ML-KEM-1024; { op: dsa-keygen | dsa-sign, seed, message } and { op: dsa-verify, …

gltf.description: a glTF 2.0 asset read as Unreal Engine reads it: { glb64 } a .glb as base64 or { json } a .gltf — what the scene holds, its extensions by prefix (KHR, EXT, vendor), loadable unless it requires an extension the GLTF_EXTENSIONS table Payload holds does not list

texts.description: many texts sealed in one call: one address per text, in the order given, and the RFC 6962 Merkle root over them with its own address, so a catalogue, a docket or a batch of records is sealed at once

brief.description: only { bytes, sha256, address } for each text, without the post-quantum and ISO blocks every full answer repeats

nist.description: true: every NIST scenario for qpu.uuidna.com.

fips180.description: FIPS 180-4: SHA-1 (160 bits), SHA-256 and SHA-512 of the text beside the fold address

sha3.description: FIPS 202: SHA3-256 and SHA3-512 of the text beside SHA-256 (textbook_sha3_fips_202)

shake.description: FIPS 202: SHAKE128 of 32 bytes and SHAKE256 of 64 bytes of the text.

kem.description: ML-KEM-512, ML-KEM-768 (true) or ML-KEM-1024 of FIPS 203, or { algorithm, seed }: a key, an encapsulation to it and its decapsulation computed here; the public key and ciphertext travel, the shared secret stays here and the answer says whether both sides agree

slh.description: SLH-DSA-SHA2-128s (true), 128f, 192s or 256s of FIPS 205, or { algorithm, seed }: the key computed here and, with text, a signature over it verified here; the s sets take seconds to sign, 128f tens of milliseconds

ed25519.description: Ed25519, RFC 8032, over the message, computed and verified here under a fresh key: true signs the text, a string is the message.

ecdsa.description: ECDSA on P-256, FIPS 186-5, over the SHA-256 of the text, computed and verified here under a fresh key.

x25519.description: X25519 Diffie–Hellman, RFC 7748: { scalar, point } as 32-byte hex each; the shared secret as hex.

pbkdf2.description: PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256, RFC 8018 / NIST SP 800-132: { password, salt, iterations, length? } — password and salt as utf-8, or hex when hex: true; length defaults to 32.

merkle.description: RFC 6962 Merkle tree over SHA-256 (Certificate Transparency): { leaves } the root; { leaves, index } the inclusion proof; { leaf, proof: [{ hash, right }], root } verifies inclusion.

constants.description: the physical constants as coins: true the request for CODATA's table (NIST, open); { text } the table read into exact integers (mantissa × 10^exponent), each constant sealed by address and SHA-256 with its stated uncertainty kept, exact ones marked; a seal proves a value is the …

key.description: HMAC key, when a keyed seal is wanted

aead.description: AES-256-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305, both ways: { cipher: aes-256-gcm | chacha20-poly1305, key, nonce, text, aad? } seals; add open: { ciphertext, tag } and the tag is checked before any text is returned.

sign.description: an ML-DSA signature over the text, computed and verified here: ML-DSA-44, ML-DSA-65 (true) or ML-DSA-87 under a fresh key, or { algorithm, seed } to sign with the key of a 32-byte seed the caller keeps

referer.description: seeds bound to a referer block: its address, or { address, chunks }; HKDF-SHA256 with the address as salt and the chunk index as info, derived here under a test key, else planned for the host, whose secret never travels; the referer adds binding, not entropy

artifacts.description: public artifacts verified against the digests their registries recorded: [{ source, name, url, algorithm, claimed, base64, status }] as the client downloaded them, the bytes hashed here by the algorithm named (npm tarballs by their sha512 integrity, Zenodo files by their …

tamper.description: { text, address, sha256? }: a copy checked against the address and digest the original carried — authentic when both match, modified when the text no longer matches them (adapted material under the licence), forged when the address matches and the digest does not (a crafted …

entropy.description: the device's randomness: samples of the animation's phase at each interaction ({ phase, t, nonce?, x?, y? }), eleven bits a phase and thirty-two a nonce, folded to a seed the text is salted with; rated by the chain (a coil beyond the first period: the fusion)

receipts.description: [{ id, leaves: [address… | { seed }], recorded }]: holds when the current fold recomputes the recorded address, stale when an earlier fold does, wrong when none does; a { seed } leaf is minted by uuidna's toUuid.

now.description: the clock (ms) the validity is judged at; absent, not judged
